title: Vegetables Highest in Iron

seo.meta_description: Raw spinach and beet greens are about 2.5–2.7 mg iron/100 g, asparagus near 2.1 mg, and Swiss chard around 1.8 mg. Plant iron is nonheme and absorption varies.
seo.search_intent: Compare iron-rich vegetables with numbers and understand plant-iron absorption.

excerpt: Among common vegetables, raw spinach provides about 2.7 mg iron per 100 g, beet greens about 2.6 mg, asparagus near 2.1 mg, and Swiss chard around 1.8 mg. These are total-iron numbers; vegetable iron is nonheme and is generally absorbed less efficiently than heme iron.
content_html:
Spinach deserves some of its iron reputation, but the story is more nuanced than a ranking. Several leafy vegetables are close, and the amount in a table is not the same as the amount your body absorbs.

Approximate raw values per 100 g

VegetableApprox. iron
Spinach~2.7 mg
Beet greens~2.6 mg
Asparagus~2.1 mg
Swiss chard~1.8 mg
Kale~1.5 mg
Broccoli~0.7 mg

Values are rounded and vary by cultivar and preparation.

Vegetable iron is nonheme iron

NIH explains that nonheme iron has more variable absorption than heme iron. Phytates and some polyphenols can inhibit absorption, while vitamin C consumed in the same meal improves it.

Serving size changes the number

A salad containing 50 g of spinach provides about 1.3 mg iron, not 2.7 mg. Adding red pepper, tomatoes, or vitamin-C-rich fruit can improve use of that nonheme iron.

Legumes are a different category

If the comparison expands beyond vegetables, lentils, beans, chickpeas, and soy are important plant iron sources and often provide more per realistic serving.

Spinach contains useful iron, but portion size, bioavailability, and the rest of the meal matter as much as the per-100-g number.

faq.question: Is spinach the highest-iron vegetable?
faq.answer: It is among the higher common vegetables at about 2.7 mg/100 g, but beet greens are very similar.

faq.question: Is plant iron absorbed like meat iron?
faq.answer: No. Nonheme iron has lower and more variable absorption than heme iron.

faq.question: What helps absorb vegetable iron?
faq.answer: Vitamin C eaten in the same meal can increase nonheme iron absorption.
